Sachkhere Oldest Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sachkhere, Georgia

Not demolished. Sachkhere's Jewish origins are disputed: the 19th-century Georgian historian Zakaria Chichinadze traced the community to Kartli, while other sources point to ongoing migration between Sachkhere and nearby Kutaisi. Some of Sachkhere's Jews were serfs during the feudal period, and because the community had no single separate district — Jews lived dispersed throughout the town — four synagogues operated, one in each district, including a wooden synagogue built in 1901 and a stone one in 1903. This, the oldest of Sachkhere's Jewish cemeteries, likely dates to around the same period and is located in the village of Zeda Skhvitori, on the road toward the Todadze fortress; its gravestones are illegible and mostly covered by soil.
